target_customer: Governments and companies sending payloads to the Moon
problem: Lunar delivery is expensive and needs dedicated launches; no lunar navigation equivalent to GPS.

founders.name: Joaquim Dickson
founders.background_notes: Worked on IMAP magnetometer and Solar Orbiter instrument.

technical_complexity.rationale: Lunar landing with custom propulsion and visual navigation; hardware and mission risk, first mission targeted Q4 2028.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware know-how and heritage; capital-intensive entry but several funded lander firms exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Peers were landing missions in 2025 (Firefly Blue Ghost landed 2025-03-02); no copying of the rideshare wedge found.

market_need_then: NASA CLPS buyers and countries lacking lander access seek low-cost delivery (Payload, 2026-06).

brand_strength.rationale: Evocative real word; no sourced brand evidence.

pivots.to: Low-cost lunar landers launched as LEO rideshare
pivots.why: CEO said launches were expensive and hard to secure, so they tackled the bigger problem (Payload, 2026-06)

outcome_analysis: Instinct Space is an early-stage London hardware startup that joined YC W25 as a lunar navigation constellation and pivoted to small landers, targeting a first mission in late 2028. It has not flown yet and no verified round beyond YC exists; hardware complexity and capital needs are the main risks.
notes: Payload (2026-06-17) says ~$1.2M raised during YC; Dealroom lists $125K at $500K valuation (2025-03); conflict, so neither recorded as a round. Competitor names come from 2025 coverage of lander peers, not sources naming Instinct's rivals at founding. Pivot date approximate. Dealroom lists 6 staff vs YC 5.
